summary: Black Hills National Forest lookout on Scruton Mountain: a 1939 log tower, a steel replacement dated 1975 (1966 in one source), still standing; the summit road is gated.

facts.design: CL-100 cab on a steel tower (current); the 1939 structure had an L-4 cab

access.note: A hiking blog reports the road gate locked and no access onto the tower itself. No Forest Service statement on public access was found.

visit.trail_note: About 1.8 miles one way from the gated road off Edelweiss Mountain Road (FS 251), per a hiking blog. Visitors reported no access to the tower.

facts.agency: US Forest Service, Black Hills National Forest

events.note: First tower completed September 1939: 30-foot log tower with a 14x14 cab.
The 1939 report said it would be manned through the fire season from the next spring. firelookout.com lists observers from 1940 to 1944.
Wooden superstructure replaced and stairs reconfigured.
A two-acre blaze half a mile from the tower, controlled by the Pactola ranger and crew.
firelookout.com dates a 67-foot all-steel live-in tower here, partly built from a 53-foot tower moved from Mt. Pisgah, Wyoming. The register and westlookouts date the steel tower to 1975.
Original wooden tower taken down with explosive charges on its legs (westlookouts) or destroyed (firelookout.com).
Current CL-100 cab and steel tower constructed a short distance from the original site.
Registered July 10, 2022 on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 1658.

corrections.why: The register describes the current cab as a CL-100 and gives the L-4 cab to the earlier 1939 structure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and westlookouts (citing a 2011 book) date the current steel tower to 1975. firelookout.com dates a 67-foot all-steel tower to 1966 and the wooden tower's destruction to 1975. The story reports both; the 1975 date has more support but is not confirmed by a Forest Service record.
Sources give 53 ft (SummitPost), 55 ft (register) and 67 ft (firelookout.com). The brief's 16.2 m matches the 53-foot figure, but height is left out of facts and flagged as unverified.
The register gives 5,817 ft (1,773 m), SummitPost gives 5,922 ft, and firelookout.com gives 5,597 ft. The record keeps 1,773 m, the register figure.

notes_for_editor: The 1966 versus 1975 steel-tower date is the main open question; a Black Hills National Forest history or a Forest Service lookout inventory would settle it. Current access rests on one hiking blog of unknown date plus a SummitPost route description; no Forest Service page for this tower was found, and the Black Hills NF page checked says five towers remain in service without naming them. No rental listing found. The brief's height_m (16.2) was left out of facts because sources conflict.
